children.text: May in Egypt is a good month. It is not an easy month.
The winter peak has passed, and the main sites are a little thinner. Hotel and cruise prices tend to come down, and the Red Sea moves into a strong season. At the same time,
Luxor
and
Aswan
turn hot. Late in the month especially, you should not build a daytime outdoor schedule with the same instincts as winter.
May is worth going. The value is not only "cheap and quiet." Morning Karnak in good light, a quieter
Valley of the Kings
, escaping into climate-controlled museums in
Cairo
in the afternoon, the Red Sea before the water peaks. May rewards travellers who can build the timetable carefully.
May's heat differs by region
Egypt does not have one climate in May.
Alexandria
, Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, and the Red Sea all feel different.
Cairo is on its way warm. Days run from around 30°C into higher, and the sun is strong. Using morning and evening well,
Giza
, Saqqara, the museums, and city sites still work.
Luxor and Aswan are different. May is already hot, and daytime is heavy. As the month progresses, afternoon site visits cost more energy. Building the Valley of the Kings, Karnak, Philae, and
Abu Simbel
into winter timing turns sightseeing into endurance.
The Red Sea works well in May.
Hurghada
, Sharm el-Sheikh, and
Marsa Alam
see warmer water — strong for diving and snorkelling. Not as oppressive as midsummer middays, not as cold as winter. Adding the sea to the trip in May is reasonable.
The Mediterranean coast also has appeal in May. Alexandria and the
Marsa Matruh
area move into the coastal season before it becomes too hot. On a first Egypt trip, set the priorities for Cairo, Luxor, Aswan, and the Red Sea before adding the Mediterranean.
A correct May day
In May, when matters as much as where.

In Luxor and Aswan, early-morning starts are the base. The Valley of the Kings, Karnak, Hatshepsut, Philae, and Abu Simbel are morning places. Not only cool — the light is good, crowds are thinner, and the form of the sites reads more clearly.
After about 11 a.m., don't pack the outdoor schedule. Return to the hotel, head to a museum, take a longer lunch, use transfer time. In a May itinerary, rest time is design, not laziness.
The evening is usable again.
Luxor Temple

, walks along the Nile, Islamic Cairo, the Aswan riverside read better in the evening. A traveller who handles May well puts mornings and evenings in the lead and uses midday for transfers and recovery.
Cairo and Giza

May in Cairo turns hot but stays workable. Go to the Giza pyramids in the morning. The plateau has little shade, and stone and sand glare back hard in the afternoon. Whether or not you take a camel or carriage, hat, water, and walking shoes are needed.

Beyond Giza, Saqqara is worth thinking about. The step pyramid, the Pyramid Texts inside Unas, and Old Kingdom tombs make clear that pyramids did not appear finished — they were the result of long experiment. In May, put Saqqara in the morning too.
The Grand Egyptian Museum is very usable in May. Sitting close to
the Giza plateau

, climate-controlled, it lets you look at ancient Egypt in depth. Following the pyramids with the museum balances outdoor and indoor. The display is large — don't try to take in everything on an exhausted afternoon.
Islamic and Coptic quarters fit the evening. Al-Muizz Street,
Khan el-Khalili
, the
Mosque of Ibn Tulun
the Hanging Church
, the Coptic Museum. They show a layer of Cairo distinct from the ancient sites. Just avoiding the hottest hours changes the experience.
Luxor
May in Luxor is harsh if you mistime the itinerary. With early movement, it rewards strongly. Winter group tours thin slightly, and the Valley of the Kings and Karnak open up quieter hours.

Go to the Valley of the Kings right at opening. Tomb interiors are narrow, and a group changes the impression of the space. For separate-ticket tombs — Ramses V and VI, Seti I, Tutankhamun — choose tombs rather than collecting them.

Karnak is also a morning place. The Great Hypostyle Hall, with light coming through the columns, reads not just as scale but as structure. Later, heat and movement of people make concentration harder.

On the west bank, the question is how to combine the Valley of the Kings with Hatshepsut, Medinet Habu, and Deir el-Medina. In May, set priorities rather than pack everything. Seeing many things under heat doesn't leave memory.
Aswan and Abu Simbel
May in Aswan is hot. It is still important. Different from Luxor's density, Aswan carries a calm pace of river, islands, granite, and Nubian culture.
Visit Philae in the morning if you can. The boat crossing is beautiful, and early light is soft and heat manageable. The Unfinished Obelisk and the Nubian Museum work into the day's design.

Abu Simbel is worth visiting in May too. Don't underestimate the transfer and the heat. Early departure from Aswan and morning visit is the base. Read the temple's scale, Ramses II's political intent, and the 1960s international relocation together, and it stops being a far day trip and becomes something else.
For Aswan in May, hotel choice matters. A place to return to and rest at midday, a place by the river for evening, a hotel that doesn't load transfers heavily — these lower the cost of the heat.
The Red Sea

The Red Sea in May is one of the easiest right choices in Egypt. Hurghada, Sharm el-Sheikh, and Marsa Alam read naturally as the season for going in the water. Warmer than winter and less oppressive than midsummer, it suits diving and snorkelling.

Sharm el-Sheikh suits travellers targeting Ras Mohammed and Strait of Tiran reefs. Hurghada has the broadest hotel range and pairs naturally with Luxor. Marsa Alam, further south, suits travellers focused on the sea itself.

Placing the May Red Sea at the end of the trip is the good move. After Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan in history, restore at the sea. With a hot season, the meaning of closing on the sea is stronger. One night is mostly transfer load — at least two, ideally three.
Sham el-Nessim
Around May, watch for Sham el-Nessim. The national spring holiday falls on the Monday after Coptic Easter and shifts year to year between late April and early May.

On the day, Egyptian families head to parks, riversides, and beaches and eat eggs, green onions, and salted fish. Not a holiday for tourists; an everyday Egyptian celebration of spring. If you happen onto it, you see another face of the country.
On a holiday, traffic crowds and some public sites and venues change hours. If your travel overlaps, confirm transfer and visit times in advance.
Ramadan and May
Ramadan follows the lunar calendar and shifts a little each year. Some years it overlaps May; some not. If you plan a May trip, check this year's Ramadan and Eid dates.

Egypt is not a country to avoid during Ramadan. Daytime eating and drinking, shop hours, museum and site hours, and traffic flow can change. After sunset, the city wakes up; old Cairo carries a particular air.

Treat it less as a constraint and more as a time when the trip's character shifts. For a first traveller uncertain about logistics, picking a date that does not overlap Ramadan makes planning simpler.
Packing and dress

In May, thin, light, sun-protective clothing helps. Breathable long sleeves, long trousers, hat, and sunglasses outperform shorts and sleeveless. Just not taking the sun directly changes how tired you become.
Shoes matter. Site footing is uneven, with sand, stone, and steps. Sandals alone at the Valley of the Kings or Saqqara tire your feet beyond the heat. Bring closed walking shoes.

Hydration runs higher than you think. The dry heat hides the sweating. Beyond water, electrolyte powders or tablets help. Sunscreen, hat, a light layer, and a layer for strong air-conditioning in cars and museums all help.
A good May itinerary
For a first trip of eight to ten days, base on Cairo, Giza, Luxor, and Aswan, and don't force in the Red Sea. Adding transfers in a hot season thins each place's impression.
With ten to twelve days, add a Hurghada stay of two to three nights at the end after Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan. History first, sea-rest last.
If the beach is the main goal, five to seven nights on the Red Sea with Luxor as a day trip or one-night addition works. From Hurghada it builds easily; from Sharm it is a different transfer.
May is not the month to see a little of everything. It is the month to choose what plays the lead, with the heat in mind.
May's conclusion
May in Egypt is not easy for everyone the way winter is. Built carefully, the quiet, the price, the light, and the sea conditions line up well.
The heat is real. So use the morning. Rest at midday. Don't pack the transfers. Put the sea at the end if you include it.
May in Egypt is harsh on people who push and quite generous to people who plan.

deck: A practical guide for travellers planning Egypt in May — the heat, the crowds, regional differences, and how to combine the Red Sea, Cairo, Luxor, and Aswan.
